title: The Globe Of The Earth Its Journey And The Proofs Of Mercy On The Page Of Spring

questions.question: What does the globe invite the traveller to do instead of continuing to roam through the sky?
questions.answer: It invites him to examine the earth’s works and learn from what it shows.

questions.question: How is the globe’s movement pictured at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It is pictured as moving like a whirling dervish with two kinds of motion.

questions.question: What results from the earth’s circling movement according to the passage?
questions.answer: It brings about the sequence of days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: How is the earth described in relation to living creatures?
questions.answer: It is described as a grand vessel carrying the provisions and tools needed by living beings.

questions.question: What does the earth’s steady condition in space suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests careful control, balance, and purposeful order.

questions.question: When the traveller studies the earth’s pages, what does he understand them to be declaring?
questions.answer: He understands them to be declaring the lordship of Allah in many clear signs.

questions.question: Which part of the earth’s “book” does the traveller focus on especially?
questions.answer: He focuses on the section about the creation and spreading of living beings in spring.

questions.question: What is striking about the emergence of many species in spring?
questions.answer: Their forms come forth from simple matter with great precision.

questions.question: How are some seeds specially treated in the passage?
questions.answer: Some are given means to travel through the air so they can spread to other places.

questions.question: What does the passage emphasize about the feeding and raising of living things?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that this is done with great care, mercy, and effectiveness.

questions.question: From what kinds of materials does the passage say many foods are brought forth?
questions.answer: They are brought forth from dry earth and from roots, seeds, and small drops of fluid that seem very similar.

questions.question: What image is used to explain how provisions are delivered every spring?
questions.answer: The earth is pictured as if it were a freight car loaded from an unseen storehouse and sent out in perfect order.

questions.question: What example is given to show special mercy toward infants?
questions.answer: Milk is provided for them through their mothers in a fitting, caring way.

questions.question: Why is this provision for babies presented as especially powerful evidence?
questions.answer: Because it shows tender care, wisdom, and mercy in a very direct and personal form.

questions.question: What larger truth does the spring scene point to beyond seasonal renewal?
questions.answer: It points to resurrection and the giving of life to the dead.

questions.question: Why does the passage call spring a living page?
questions.answer: Because it displays countless active signs of life, renewal, and divine mercy.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveller reach from the earth’s pages as a whole?
questions.answer: He concludes that the earth, through all its parts, proclaims the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: How do the details in spring support belief in divine power?
questions.answer: They show that bringing life from what seemed dead, feeding creatures, and organizing countless species all require unlimited power and wisdom.

questions.question: What change in direction is made at the beginning of the marked passage?
questions.answer: Attention shifts from the sky to the earth, which now addresses the traveller.

questions.question: What does the earth say it will show the traveller?
questions.answer: It says it will show him what he has been seeking.

questions.question: What does the phrase about reading the earth’s pages suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the earth can be studied like a meaningful text full of signs.

questions.question: What two motions of the globe are mentioned?
questions.answer: The passage refers to a double movement of the earth.

questions.question: What time-patterns are linked to the earth’s motion?
questions.answer: The passage links it to the alternation of days, the passing of years, and the changing of seasons.

questions.question: In what way is the earth compared to a ship?
questions.answer: It is compared to a huge ship carrying supplies for all living things while moving through space.

questions.question: What quality of the earth’s movement in space receives special attention?
questions.answer: Its remarkable stability and balance receive special attention.

questions.question: Which single page does he choose to study more closely?
questions.answer: He chooses the page of spring, especially the appearance of living things in it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the origin of many living forms?
questions.answer: It says they come out of simple material with exactness and distinction.

questions.question: What happens to some seeds after they are given “wings”?
questions.answer: They are spread to different places through the air.

questions.question: Besides being spread out, how are living things treated?
questions.answer: They are nourished and raised with careful attention.

questions.question: What does the variety of foods coming from similar-looking sources show?
questions.answer: It shows rich creativity and wise planning in provision.

questions.question: What is meant by food and equipment being loaded from an unseen treasury?
questions.answer: It means the provisions of spring come from a hidden source of mercy beyond visible human control.

questions.question: How does the example of mothers feeding infants deepen the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives a clear, intimate example of compassion and wisdom built into creation.

questions.question: What connection is made between spring and the revival of the dead?
questions.answer: Spring is presented as an observable example that makes resurrection easier to understand.

questions.question: What is the final testimony the traveller hears from the earth?
questions.answer: He hears that all its pages, each in its own way, declare that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: Why does the globe tell the traveller to stop wandering through the heavens?
questions.answer: Because the signs he is searching for can also be found clearly in the earth itself.

questions.question: What does the earth’s movement establish according to the passage?
questions.answer: It establishes the regular order of time through days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the image of a ship important for understanding the earth?
questions.answer: It highlights that the earth carries and delivers what living creatures need.

questions.question: What does the phrase about food and equipment for animate beings imply?
questions.answer: It implies that provision on earth is broad, intentional, and suited to many forms of life.

questions.question: What does the traveller realize about the earth’s chapters and pages?
questions.answer: He realizes they are full of signs pointing to the Sustainer.

questions.question: Why is spring especially suitable for close study in this passage?
questions.answer: Because spring visibly gathers many examples of creation, nourishment, and renewal in one season.

questions.question: What is remarkable about the production of species from simple material?
questions.answer: Distinct and complex forms appear from something outwardly plain and limited.

questions.question: What function do the airborne seeds serve in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: They show that even distribution and reproduction are handled with wisdom and planning.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the care given to living beings after their creation?
questions.answer: It describes them as being distributed, fed, and raised with precision and mercy.

questions.question: What contrast is highlighted in the production of food?
questions.answer: Abundant and appealing nourishment comes from dry soil and from sources that seem nearly alike.

questions.question: What does the yearly arrival of provisions in spring suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests repeated, dependable generosity from a hidden source.

questions.question: How is maternal milk used as a sign in the passage?
questions.answer: It is used as a direct sign of compassion, generosity, and wise design for the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does the quoted verse about reviving the earth support?
questions.answer: It supports the claim that the One who revives dead land can also revive the dead.

questions.question: In what sense is spring called a demonstration?
questions.answer: It serves as a visible, concrete proof of truths that people might otherwise treat as unseen or distant.

questions.question: What does the traveller conclude from all the earth’s pages, not just spring?
questions.answer: He concludes that the whole earth bears witness to divine oneness.

questions.question: Which qualities of Allah are especially emphasized in this passage through the signs of earth?
questions.answer: Mercy, generosity, wisdom, power, and sustaining care are especially emphasized.

questions.question: What invitation begins the target passage?
questions.answer: The traveller is invited to learn from the earth rather than keep roaming through the skies.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the earth’s motion in a vivid way?
questions.answer: It portrays the earth as turning like a spiritually enraptured whirling figure.

questions.question: What does the earth’s motion organize for life in the world?
questions.answer: It organizes the rhythms of time such as days, years, and seasons.

questions.question: Why is the earth called magnificent in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it carries vast provisions for countless living beings while moving in ordered balance.

questions.question: What does floating in space with balance imply about the earth?
questions.answer: It implies that its condition is governed with precision rather than left to disorder.

questions.question: What does the traveller notice when he examines the earth as if it were a written work?
questions.answer: He notices that its parts are full of signs pointing to its Lord.

questions.question: Why does he focus on animate beings in spring?
questions.answer: Because spring gives a concentrated display of life being brought forth and sustained.

questions.question: What does “countless members of hundreds of thousands of species” stress?
questions.answer: It stresses the immense variety and scale of life.

questions.question: What can students infer from forms appearing with precision from simple material?
questions.answer: That their formation is intentional and guided by exact knowledge.

questions.question: What is the significance of some seeds being enabled to travel?
questions.answer: It shows that spreading life across the earth happens through ordered means.

questions.question: How does the passage combine mercy and organization in describing spring?
questions.answer: It shows that living things are not only created but also carefully supplied, distributed, and raised.

questions.question: What does the emergence of many foods from dry earth and similar substances indicate?
questions.answer: It indicates a power that brings rich variety out of seemingly limited materials.

questions.question: Why is the comparison to a railway car effective?
questions.answer: It makes the yearly delivery of provisions feel systematic, loaded, and sent out with order.

questions.question: What example especially highlights compassion toward the weakest creatures?
questions.answer: The fitting provision of milk for babies through their mothers especially highlights that compassion.

questions.question: How does this example support belief in mercy as a divine attribute?
questions.answer: It shows tender care reaching creatures at the moment they need it most.

questions.question: What truth about the afterlife is illustrated by spring in the passage?
questions.answer: Spring illustrates that bringing life back after apparent death is fully within divine power.

questions.question: Why is spring called tangible evidence?
questions.answer: Because it offers something visible and experienced directly, not just an abstract claim.

questions.question: What central declaration does the traveller hear from the earth’s pages?
questions.answer: He hears the declaration of Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the globe promise the traveller at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It promises to show him the reality he has been searching for.

questions.question: What method of learning is the traveller urged to use regarding the earth?
questions.answer: He is urged to observe its functions and read its signs.

questions.question: How is the earth’s movement described in relation to the larger created order?
questions.answer: It is described as drawing a great cycle within a wider field of gathering.

questions.question: Which recurring patterns of earthly life come from this movement?
questions.answer: The recurring patterns include day and night cycles, the yearly cycle, and seasonal changes.

questions.question: How does the ship image shape the reader’s understanding of the earth?
questions.answer: It presents the earth as a carrier of life-supporting resources for all creatures.

questions.question: What does the phrase about hundreds of thousands of kinds of provision suggest about creation?
questions.answer: It suggests abundance, diversity, and careful preparation.

questions.question: What does the traveller discover when he looks at the earth’s pages?
questions.answer: He discovers that they point again and again to the Sustainer.

questions.question: Why does he narrow his attention to springtime life?
questions.answer: Because spring offers a clear display of creation, renewal, and sustenance.

questions.question: What is the relationship between simple matter and living form in the passage?
questions.answer: Simple matter becomes the source from which highly distinct living forms appear.

questions.question: How do flying seeds function as evidence in the argument?
questions.answer: They show planned dispersal and effective continuation of life.

questions.question: What three processes of care are stressed after creatures appear?
questions.answer: Their spreading, feeding, and nurturing are all stressed.

questions.question: What makes the production of food especially impressive in the passage?
questions.answer: Many pleasing and useful foods come from plain earth and from materials that seem almost the same.

questions.question: How often does the loading of provision onto the earth occur according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as happening every spring.

questions.question: What does the “unseen treasury” idea imply about the source of provision?
questions.answer: It implies that the true source lies beyond visible material causes alone.

questions.question: Why is milk for infants singled out rather than treated as just one more food?
questions.answer: Because it is a deeply personal sign of mercy, tenderness, and wise suitability.

questions.question: What does the verse about reviving the earth help the traveller understand?
questions.answer: It helps him understand that the One who revives dead land can also resurrect human beings.

questions.question: How does spring act as a sample of the greater gathering to come?
questions.answer: It gathers innumerable living forms back into appearance after a season of lifelessness.

questions.question: What final creed-like understanding does the traveller gain from the earth?
questions.answer: He understands that the earth in all its parts testifies that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: Who speaks first in the marked passage, and what is the effect of that choice?
questions.answer: The globe speaks first, and this makes the earth seem like a witness and guide.

questions.question: What does the globe want the traveller to stop doing?
questions.answer: It wants him to stop searching only in the heights above.

questions.question: What does the globe offer in place of that wandering?
questions.answer: It offers its own works and signs as a source of understanding.

questions.question: What is emphasized by describing the globe with two motions?
questions.answer: It emphasizes that the earth’s movement is complex yet ordered.

questions.question: What order of life is tied to those motions?
questions.answer: The regular order of days, years, and seasons is tied to them.

questions.question: In what way is the earth portrayed as serving animate beings?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as carrying their food and necessities like a carefully managed vessel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the earth’s balanced travel in space?
questions.answer: That such steadiness points to deliberate governance.

questions.question: What does the traveller understand from the earth’s many pages?
questions.answer: He understands that they are full of testimonies to the One who sustains the earth.

questions.question: What seasonal page does he focus on, and why?
questions.answer: He focuses on spring because it vividly displays life’s return and distribution.

questions.question: What makes the emergence of species in spring so meaningful?
questions.answer: Vast numbers of distinct creatures appear from basic material with exact order.

questions.question: How does the passage connect seeds to movement and spread?
questions.answer: It says some are equipped to travel so they can be scattered widely.

questions.question: What does careful feeding and nurturing add to the argument beyond creation itself?
questions.answer: It shows that divine care continues after life begins, not just at its first appearance.

questions.question: Why is the origin of many foods from plain substances important?
questions.answer: It shows that rich provision comes from simple means through wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: What does the yearly loading of supplies in spring reveal about the world?
questions.answer: It reveals an ongoing system of provision that is ordered and dependable.

questions.question: How is the feeding of infants presented as a special sign?
questions.answer: It is presented as a tender and wise arrangement that perfectly meets their need.

questions.question: What major doctrine is supported by the reviving of the earth after winter?
questions.answer: It supports belief in resurrection.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It starts with visible features of the earth and ends with a declaration of divine oneness.

questions.question: If you had to state the main message of the whole marked passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: The earth, especially in spring, shows through order, provision, and renewal that Allah alone is the all-powerful and merciful Sustainer.
